clue.text: No, I don't aim in any way to gain control

indicators.note: in any way says the letters of the preceding words may be taken in any order you like

explanation.surface: Someone protests that they have no ambition to take charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in any way' tells you to rearrange the ten letters of NO, I DON'T AIM; 'to gain' simply links the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Domination is mastery or power held over others, a synonym of control used as a noun.

clue.text: Love game

definitions.meaning: a familiar British term of endearment, 'love', has the slang equivalent you would call a friend in northern England
game here means wild birds shot for sport or food

explanation.walkthrough: In the north of England people address each other as 'duck' the way others say 'love'; a duck is also a wildfowl shot as game.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are synonyms: a regional endearment like 'dear', and a wildfowl hunted for sport.

clue.text: Intends to examine benefit claimants

parts.note: intends means 'means', as in 'he means to go'
to examine is to test

explanation.surface: An official plans to look closely into people claiming welfare payments.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the answer: a check of claimants' income before benefit is paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A means test is an official inquiry into someone's income and savings to decide whether they qualify for state support.

clue.text: Trim for a sober gent in New York

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: taken as written
TT, teetotal, describes a sober person who never drinks

explanation.surface: A neat outfit suits a man who doesn't drink, living in Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: TT (teetotal) is the crossword convention for someone who abstains from alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Trim as an adjective means neat and smart in appearance, a close synonym.

clue.text: Causing vexation by combing

definitions.meaning: annoying someone by mocking or provoking them
drawing out or fluffing up fibres or hair with a comb

explanation.walkthrough: To tease is both to annoy playfully and to comb wool or backcomb hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Provoking someone with jibes and raising the nap of fibres with a comb are both called by this word.

clue.text: Set up company to store grain produced naturally

definitions.note: the definition is an adverb while the answer is an adjective, as in 'grown naturally' versus 'grown in an organic way'

indicators.note: to store means the preceding piece holds the following letters inside it
in a down clue set up means the word is written upwards, so read backwards
produced suggests the letters are brought out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A business is founded to stockpile cereal from a farm that avoids chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' turns CO into OC; 'produced' rearranges GRAIN into RGANI, which 'to store' places inside OC.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is grown without artificial chemicals, in a natural way.

clue.text: Separate section

definitions.meaning: to divide or move apart, a verb
a portion or piece of a whole, a noun

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a verb, to split up; the other a noun, a portion.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide things is to split them, and a piece of a whole is a portion: both senses share one word.

clue.text: Vital for a criminal to be sent back

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: sent back tells you to write the word for criminal in reverse

parts.note: criminal as an adjective can mean wicked, evil

explanation.surface: It is essential that a wrongdoer be deported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be sent back' turns EVIL into LIVE, which follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital in its root sense means living, full of life.

clue.text: Patrolmen ordered to imprison one bouncer

indicators.note: to imprison means the rearranged letters lock the next piece inside them
ordered suggests the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Police officers are instructed to lock up a nightclub doorman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges PATROLMEN; 'to imprison' puts I inside, after TRAMPOL. 'Bouncer' looks like a doorman but is something you bounce on.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampoline is a sprung frame used for jumping, so it is something that makes people spring up and down.

clue.text: Drink and dance

definitions.meaning: a cocktail of advocaat and lemonade popular in Britain
a dance where couples keep splitting to bring in new partners until all are dancing

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is a Christmas cocktail of advocaat and lemonade, and also a party dance whose numbers grow as each dancer fetches a new partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are named after something that grows as it rolls: a festive mixed cocktail and a party dance that keeps adding people.

clue.text: Carol may not catch Henry

indicators.note: catch means the preceding word holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: can't means is not allowed to, may not
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A girl called Carol is unable to grab a boy called Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' reads as a woman's name but is a song; H (henry, unit of inductance) goes inside CANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To carol is to sing joyfully, and a chant is a sung or intoned song or refrain.

clue.text: French money in a S. American state

parts.note: argent is the French word for money (and silver)
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Euros are being spent somewhere in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: ARGENT is French for money, from the word for silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a country in South America.

clue.text: The came down like the wolf on the fold (Byron)

definitions.text: The came down like the wolf on the fold (Byron)

parts.words: The came down like the wolf on the fold (Byron)
parts.note: a quotation from Byron's poem on Sennacherib with its subject left out: fill the gap with the invading people

explanation.walkthrough: Byron's poem 'The Destruction of Sennacherib' opens with this line about the ancient Mesopotamian army attacking Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Byron's line is the nationality of Sennacherib's invading army from ancient Mesopotamia.

clue.text: Puppy requires women's assistance

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
assistance means help

explanation.surface: A young dog needs looking after by the ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: W for women is a standard abbreviation; 'requires' links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A whelp is a young dog, a pup or cub.

clue.text: Author describing northern city with style

parts.note: Chester is a city in the north-west of England, in Cheshire
ton means fashion or style, from French

explanation.surface: A writer gives a stylish account of a city in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: CHESTER is an English city in Cheshire; TON is an old word for high fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: G. K. Chesterton was an English writer, creator of the Father Brown detective stories.

clue.text: Listing work done by a cobbler

definitions.meaning: a ship that is listing leans over to one side
a shoe repairer fixes new pieces onto the backs of shoes

explanation.walkthrough: A ship heels over when it tilts; a cobbler heels shoes by replacing their backs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilting to one side at sea and fitting new backs to shoes share the same word.

clue.text: Doing nothing but fighting

definitions.meaning: read as two words, engaged in battle

explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN ACTION the answer means engaged in combat; as one word it means idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is the plain sense; split in two, the phrase describes soldiers engaged in combat.

clue.text: Risk getting left behind the nave

definitions.note: the definition is a descriptive phrase for a part of a church, standing for the noun

parts.note: to risk something is to chance it

explanation.surface: A gambler leaves something behind in the middle of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: In a church the nave is the main body; the area beyond it, around the altar, is the chancel.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancel is the part of a church near the altar, east of the main body where the congregation sits.

clue.text: Can't Irish convert declare his faith?

definitions.text: Can't Irish convert declare his faith?

indicators.note: convert as a verb means change, so the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Is a new believer from Ireland unable to state his religion?
explanation.walkthrough: 'convert' rearranges CANT IRISH; the whole clue also describes a believer in the Irish context, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Jesus would declare himself one when asked about his religion.

clue.text: A group just likely to succeed

parts.note: a set is a group of things or people
just means fair, even-handed

explanation.surface: A band of people with a decent chance of making it.
explanation.walkthrough: SET FAIR is a weather-forecast phrase for settled fine weather, extended to mean poised for success.
explanation.definitionFit: Set fair describes conditions favourable for good outcome, as in weather settled and fine.

clue.text: Stay for ceremony incorporating clairvoyance

indicators.note: incorporating means the ceremony word takes the next letters into its body

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
ESP, extrasensory perception, covers clairvoyance

explanation.surface: Delay a ritual that involves fortune-telling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' is the legal sense, a stay of execution, not remaining somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay of execution is a postponement or reprieve.

clue.text: Civil War battles causing stock-market boom

definitions.meaning: two battles of the American Civil War fought near Manassas, Virginia
a period of rising share prices

explanation.walkthrough: The First and Second Battles of Bull Run were fought in Virginia; a bull market is one where prices rise.
explanation.definitionFit: The American battles named after a Virginia creek, and a sustained rise in share prices, share the name.

clue.text: Train bishop to use the phone

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to ring up is to telephone someone

explanation.surface: A bishop is taught how to make a telephone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' is a verb here, to rear or educate, not a railway train.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up a child is to rear and educate them.

clue.text: Quite right to demand payment

definitions.meaning: to insist on and extract money owed, a verb

explanation.walkthrough: As an adjective it means precise; as a verb it means to demand and obtain, as in exacting a toll.
explanation.definitionFit: Precise correctness and the forcible collection of a payment are both expressed by this word.

clue.text: Other name for a return voyage

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: return tells you to turn the word for voyage backwards

parts.note: a sail is a trip in a boat, a voyage

explanation.surface: The name given for a round trip by sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses SAIL into LIAS, which follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is an assumed or alternative name.

clue.text: Bookkeeper acquires petticoat and suit

parts.note: a slip is a petticoat worn under a dress
a suit in court is a case

explanation.surface: An accountant buys underwear and a business outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookkeeper' wants to be an accountant, but it is literally a holder for a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-case is a protective box that holds a book, so it literally keeps books.

clue.text: The jacket is just about finished

parts.note: C, from circa, is the abbreviation for about
finished means over

explanation.surface: The book's dust wrapper is nearly done.
explanation.walkthrough: C for circa (about) is a standard abbreviation; a book's jacket is its cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust jacket wraps a book, as a protective outer layer does.

clue.text: Initially taken into consideration, as is fair

indicators.note: into means the first letter goes inside the word for consideration

parts.note: consideration can mean a payment for services, a fee

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A point is first weighed up, as is only just.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consideration' is the payment sense, a fee, not careful thought; 'Initially' gives T from 'taken'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fête is an outdoor event with stalls and games, much like a fair.

clue.text: Ensuring that people are well suited

definitions.text: Ensuring that people are well suited

parts.words: Ensuring that people are well suited
parts.note: reads as matchmaking compatible partners, but means making clothes that fit their wearers

explanation.definitionFit: The craft of cutting and fitting garments makes sure clients are dressed in well-fitting suits.

clue.text: Articulate deputy admits nothing

indicators.note: admits means the word for deputy lets the next letter in

parts.note: vice, as in vice-president, means deputy
O, the digit zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: An eloquent second-in-command confesses to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' looks like an adjective for the deputy but is the verb, to express.
explanation.definitionFit: To articulate an opinion is to express it, to give it utterance.

clue.text: Some of the merino sheep need food

definitions.note: the definition is a verb phrase; the answer as a verb means to eat

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the flock of woolly sheep are hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'merino sheep'. NOSH is British slang for food or for eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for food, and as a verb means to eat.

clue.text: Under hypnosis English MEP displayed restraint

indicators.note: under hypnosis means inside a trance, so the next pieces go inside that word

parts.note: a hypnotised person is in a trance

indicators.note: displayed suggests the letters are laid out in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A hypnotised British Euro-politician showed self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed' rearranges MEP into MPE; E plus MPE goes inside TRANCE ('Under' as in under a trance).
explanation.definitionFit: Temperance is moderation or self-control, especially abstinence from alcohol.
